newsitem.title: USA: Ford to purchase stadium rights for $40 mln.
newsitem.headline: Ford to purchase stadium rights for $40 mln.

text.p: Ford Motor Co said Friday it has purchased the right to place its name on a new downtown Detroit domed stadium for $40 million.
Ford said the fee is payable over several years. The agreement also includes other marketing rights, the company said.
The 70,000-seat stadium will be home to the Detroit Lions football team. It will also be used for other athletic and entertainment events and conventions.
"The value of having your company's name associated with a high-profile athletic facility is extraordinary," said Ford chairman Alex Trotman in a statement.
Construction of the stadium is subject to approval of a tax on hotels and rental cars in Wayne County, where the stadium will be located. The tax will be voted on November 5.

The Lions face a November 1 deadline to gain committments for $50 million in corporate and private contributions, needed to put the tax on the ballot. Ford said the city assured the company that remaining corporate investments will be received.
